title: A Practical Guide for Supporting Formative Assessment and Feedback Using Generative AI
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how generative AI, especially large language models such as ChatGPT, can be aligned with the core pedagogical principles of formative assessment and feedback. The authors argue that much existing work on AI in education emphasizes technical performance or automation, but often misses the formative purpose of helping learners understand where they are, where they are going, and how to move forward.

Rather than reporting an empirical intervention study, the paper offers a narrative, practice-oriented framework. It organizes discussion around three formative assessment functions: clarifying learning goals, diagnosing where the learner is, and providing feedback that moves learning forward. Within each, it shows how generic LLMs, domain-specialized LLMs, and LLM-integrated educational technologies can be used through prompting to rewrite learning objectives in student-friendly language, co-construct success criteria, generate exemplars or sample work, create diagnostic questions and MCQs, and produce different levels of feedback.

The paper focuses on classroom educational practice, especially K-12 and higher-education teaching scenarios, but it does not present a participant sample, implementation trial, or direct comparative evaluation. Its main conclusion is that LLMs can augment formative assessment at scale, but only when used with teacher expertise, pedagogical judgment, and careful prompt design. The authors also emphasize that future research should develop better metrics for formative feedback quality and create pedagogically grounded prompt templates and evaluation frameworks.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative/practical review rather than an empirical study, and it does not report a systematic methodology, comparison design, or primary outcome data. It is peer-reviewed scholarly commentary, but not causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has potentially broad relevance for K-12 teacher planning and feedback workflows, but it reports no measured impact on student or teacher outcomes. Its contribution is conceptual and practice-oriented rather than demonstrably outcome-changing.

interventions.use_case: Narrative review and practical guidance on using generic LLMs like ChatGPT to support formative assessment tasks such as rewriting learning objectives, generating classroom discussion prompts, creating sample work, and producing feedback that helps students move forward.
Using LLMs to generate task-, process-, and self-regulation-level feedback on student work, including examples for code, essays, and methods sections, as part of formative assessment cycles.
